solar-calculator-method.title: How the Solar Calculator Works: Method and Assumptions
solar-calculator-method.description: How the calculator estimates system size, generation, savings and payback: postcode sunshine from SAP 10.3, degradation, self-consumption and export.
solar-calculator-method.lead: What goes into the numbers, where the data comes from, and what the calculator deliberately leaves out.
faqs: How accurate is the calculator?

It is a first estimate, not a design. Generation uses published regional sunshine data for a typical layout, so a south-facing roof may do better and a shaded one worse. Savings depend most on the share of solar you use on site and your unit price, so check those two inputs carefully. A site survey and your half-hourly meter data turn it into a firm figure.
Where does the sunshine data come from?
From SAP 10.3, the Standard Assessment Procedure used across UK building regulations. It gives monthly sunshine for 21 UK regions and maps postcode districts to them.
Why does my postcode matter?

Annual generation varies by about a third across the UK, from around 780 kWh per kWp in Shetland to over 1,050 in Southern England on the same layout. Using your postcode puts you in the right SAP region.
Does the calculator include VAT?
No. All costs are shown before VAT. Commercial installations are charged VAT at the standard 20%, which VAT-registered organisations can normally recover.
Can I see the cost rates and PPA rates behind the results?

The calculator shows your total installed cost and your indicative PPA rate. The underlying benchmarks are reviewed regularly and are not published, because real prices depend on site, scale and timing. A survey gives you a firm price.

solar-cost.title: How Much Does Commercial Solar Cost in the UK?
solar-cost.description: Installed cost per kWp for pitched roof, flat roof, ground mount and solar carports, what the price includes and excludes, and a worked example.
solar-cost.h1: How much does commercial solar cost?
solar-cost.lead: Cost per kWp by mount type, what is and is not included, and what moves the price.
faqs: How much does commercial solar cost per kWp?

Between about £900 and £1,500 per kWp installed, depending on how it is mounted. Pitched roof is cheapest at around £900 per kWp, flat roof around £1,000, ground mount around £1,050 and solar carports around £1,500. Larger systems come in below these rates and small ones above.
Can I reclaim the VAT on commercial solar?

VAT-registered businesses can normally recover VAT on a commercial solar installation in the usual way, so the figures in our calculator are shown excluding VAT. The zero rate that applies to domestic installations does not apply to commercial projects.
What is not included in the installed cost?

Roof repairs or strengthening, any grid reinforcement your network operator charges for, battery storage, finance costs and VAT. Roof condition and grid reinforcement are the two that most often change a project's economics, and both are site-specific.

solar-payback.title: How Long Does Commercial Solar Take to Pay Back?
solar-payback.description: Typical payback for UK commercial solar, the five things that move it, and a worked example for a 509 kWp warehouse roof with the full figures.
solar-payback.h1: How long does commercial solar take to pay back?
solar-payback.lead: What payback means, what changes it, and a worked example with real numbers.
faqs: How long does commercial solar take to pay back?

Most UK commercial rooftop systems pay back in roughly four to eight years. The worked example on this page, a 509 kWp warehouse roof at 25p/kWh using 80% of its generation on site, pays back in 4.9 years. Sites with a lower electricity price, less daytime demand or less sunshine take longer.
Is payback the right way to judge a solar investment?

It is a useful first filter but an incomplete one. Payback ignores everything that happens after you break even, which for a 25-year asset is where most of the value sits. Net benefit over the life of the system, and return on investment, are better measures for comparing solar against other uses of the same capital.
Does a battery make payback faster?

Usually not. A battery increases the share of generation you use on site, which increases total savings, but it also adds capital cost. In most commercial cases it raises lifetime savings while lengthening payback. The calculator lets you model it both ways.

solar-planning-and-grid.title: Commercial Solar Planning Permission and Grid Connection
solar-planning-and-grid.description: UK commercial solar hurdles: DNO grid connection under G98 and G99, export limits, permitted development, planning, roof condition and leases.
solar-planning-and-grid.h1: Planning, grid connection and other hurdles
solar-planning-and-grid.lead: What can slow down or stop a commercial solar project, and how to deal with each issue early.
faqs: Do I need planning permission for solar panels on a commercial roof?

In England, usually not. Rooftop solar on non-domestic buildings is permitted development with no capacity limit since December 2023. Listed buildings, sites with an Article 4 direction and some protected areas are exceptions. Check with your local planning authority.
Do solar carports need planning permission?
In England, canopies over non-domestic car parks can be permitted development if they are no more than 4 metres high and at least 10 metres from homes, but you must apply for prior approval first.
What is a G99 application?

G99 is the technical standard for connecting generation of more than 16A per phase to the distribution network. Almost every commercial solar system needs a G99 application and approval from the DNO before it is connected.
How long does DNO approval take?
For a typical rooftop system, allow around 12 weeks for a connection offer. It can take longer where the local network is constrained or reinforcement is needed.
What if the DNO will not let me export?

You can often accept an export limit, with a control system that stops the system sending more than an agreed amount to the grid. If your site uses most of its own solar, the lost export income is usually small.

paying-for-solar.title: How to Fund Commercial Solar: Buy, Finance, Lease or PPA
paying-for-solar.description: How UK organisations pay for solar: buying outright, asset finance, leasing and PPAs, plus tax allowances, VAT, business rates and public funding.
paying-for-solar.h1: How to pay for commercial solar
paying-for-solar.lead: Buying outright, asset finance, leasing and Power Purchase Agreements compared, with the tax and public funding rules that apply in 2026.
faqs: Can I claim 100% tax relief on solar panels?

Yes, through the Annual Investment Allowance, which covers up to £1 million of qualifying spend a year for most businesses. Companies can alternatively claim the 50% first-year allowance for special rate assets. Full expensing does not apply to solar panels because they are special rate assets.
Do I pay VAT on commercial solar?
Yes, at the standard 20% rate. VAT-registered organisations can normally reclaim it.
Will solar increase my business rates?
Not in England until at least 31 March 2035. On-site renewable generation and batteries used with it are exempt from 1 April 2022 to 31 March 2035.
What happens at the end of a PPA?
It depends on the contract. Most commercial PPAs transfer the system to you at the end, at no or low cost, so the electricity becomes free. Some offer an extension or removal instead.
Is a PPA cheaper than buying?
Over the system's life, no. Buying gives a higher total return because you keep all the savings. A PPA trades some of that return for no upfront cost and no maintenance responsibility.

solar-generation.title: How Much Electricity Will Commercial Solar Generate?
solar-generation.description: Annual generation per kWp for each UK region, where the SAP 10.3 figures come from, and how to turn roof area into kilowatt hours.
solar-generation.h1: How much electricity will commercial solar generate?
solar-generation.lead: Yield by region, the data behind it, and how to get from roof area to kilowatt hours.
faqs: How much electricity does 1 kWp of solar generate in the UK?

Between about 845 and 1,025 kWh a year, depending on location. The UK average used by our calculator is 905 kWh per kWp per year. Scotland is at the lower end at around 845, and the South West at the upper end at around 1,025. These are net figures, already adjusted for real-world losses.
How much does a 500 kWp commercial system generate?

Around 452,500 kWh a year at UK average sunshine, rising to about 512,500 kWh in the South West and falling to about 422,500 kWh in Scotland. Over 25 years, allowing for panel degradation, a 500 kWp system produces roughly 10.7 million kWh.
Does solar work in winter and on cloudy days?

Yes, but at much lower output. Panels respond to daylight rather than heat or direct sun, so they generate under cloud. A UK array typically produces around ten times as much in June as in December, with roughly three quarters of annual output falling between March and September.
